features.summary: Firefox’s media backends can better adapt video encoding while it is running, including changing bitrate and frame rate, and Android’s FFmpeg and MediaCodec paths gain improved support for H.264 and HEVC. The changes also refine low-latency decoding and hardware-decoder output, and make GPU-process and Vulkan Video checks more reliable—helping playback and encoding work smoothly across devices.

patches.author: Matthew Gregan
patches.subject: Pop the change index before performing block I/O in FileBlockCache.

features.summary: Firefox’s audio and video seeking recovery now avoids competing seeks when a reset or retry is already positioning a track, reducing the chance of playback getting out of step. The changes also adjust file-cache I/O ordering and back out a network-related AAC metadata change that caused loading to stall; media guidance for AI contributors was added as well.

features.summary: These changes add focused C++ tests for media edge cases, including video frame dimensions and image-plane layouts, audio resampling limits, and invalid audio-packet input. They help catch problems with unusual or malformed media data before those issues reach users.

features.summary: On Android, Firefox now prefers the GPU process for media decoding and encoding, including when a content decryption module (CDM) is involved in protected playback. It also waits for that process to restart before creating remote media components, and improves how remote video decode failures are reported.

features.summary: Web Audio now starts the timing graph for an autoplay-blocked AudioContext using the system clock, helping audio processing keep the right timing without changing autoplay permissions. New and re-enabled tests cover resampling audio from a low-rate media element and verify behavior across build types.

features.summary: Firefox’s Gecko Media Plugins (GMP), which support media features such as protected playback, now use cleaner origin matching and connect process information for Android plugin processes. These changes improve how plugin identity and process details are handled.

features.label: Fake Cdm

patches.author: Simon Chopin
patches.subject: Test that GMP crashes produce a minidump

features.summary: A test now verifies that a crash in a Gecko Media Plugin (GMP) produces a minidump, a small diagnostic record used to investigate crashes. This improves crash-reporting coverage without changing normal playback behavior.

features.summary: A Media Source Extensions (MSE) test that had been skipped on coverage-instrumented builds is enabled again after passing there. MSE lets websites assemble and stream media in pieces; this change improves test coverage, not playback behavior.

features.label: Tests

features.summary: Firefox now runs more Android rendering tests, called reftests, when using an isolated process. This broadens test coverage for that setup without changing browser behavior.
